newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes Thai prime minister, hails ties.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes Thai prime minister, hails ties.

text.p: China on Wednesday hailed its relations with Thailand as it put out the welcome mat for visiting Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.

"Political relations between the two countries have always been quite good and cooperation in economic, cultural and other spheres has been smooth," state television quoted Premier Li Peng as telling his Thai counterpart.

"China places great emphasis on relations with Thailand and cooperation with every nation in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)," Li told Chavalit, who arrived in the Chinese capital on Wednesday.
Li said he hoped ASEAN would aid the cause of regional and world peace.
ASEAN includes Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam as well as Thailand.
The group has been wary of China's growing military might and is nervous that Beijing's claims of sovereignty in the South China Sea could lead to regional clashes.
Li and Chavalit also signed an agreement allowing Thailand to maintain its consulate in Hong Kong after China regains sovereignty over the territory from Britain on July 1, the report said.
Li welcomed Thai investment in China and met a delegation of Thai entrepreneurs accompanying Chavalit, television said.
Chavalit was quoted as saying Bangkok was eager to attract Chinese firms to Thailand.
